l4_steps.name: Extract competitive schedule & capacity data
l4_steps.input: Annual planning cycle trigger; prior-year SSIM schedules
l4_steps.output: Competitor capacity matrix by O&D market (seats, frequencies, ASMs)
l4_steps.kpi: Market coverage: ≥95% of OAG universe validated within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: OAG data lags 48–72 hrs for LCC schedule changes; analyst must reconcile against GDS live availability

l4_steps.name: Ingest historical O&D traffic & yield data
l4_steps.input: 3-year rolling MIDT booking data, internal ticket coupon data
l4_steps.output: O&D demand baseline with seasonality indices per market pair
l4_steps.kpi: Demand model R² ≥0.90 vs actual bookings on back-test
l4_steps.pain_point: MIDT coverage drops to ~60% for LCC-heavy markets where GDS penetration is low; distorts baseline

l4_steps.name: Validate & cleanse market intelligence dataset
l4_steps.input: OAG capacity matrix, SkyCAST O&D baseline, macroeconomic indices
l4_steps.output: Validated market intelligence dataset approved for modelling
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness ≥98% of target O&D pairs before model run
l4_steps.pain_point: Macro data (GDP, tourism forecasts) sourced from multiple external vendors with inconsistent update cycles

l4_steps.name: Generate long-haul & medium-haul demand scenarios
l4_steps.input: Validated market intelligence dataset; strategic growth targets from CEO brief
l4_steps.output: 3 demand scenarios (base, upside, downside) per O&D market for 3-year horizon
l4_steps.kpi: Scenario variance within ±15% of base-case for primary markets
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM scenario runtime scales poorly for networks >500 O&D pairs; overnight batch required for full network runs

l4_steps.name: Score and rank route opportunities by strategic fit
l4_steps.input: 3 demand scenarios, strategic priority filters (geography, alliance fit, connectivity)
l4_steps.output: Ranked route opportunity scorecard (revenue potential, strategic score, competitive intensity)
l4_steps.kpi: Top-20 route list updated within 2 weeks of scenario generation
l4_steps.pain_point: Scoring weights for 'strategic fit' are subjective; senior stakeholders override quantitative ranking without documented rationale

l4_steps.name: Review route shortlist against network strategy guardrails
l4_steps.input: Ranked route opportunity scorecard, board-approved network strategy KPIs
l4_steps.output: Approved route shortlist (10–30 routes) for feasibility analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Shortlist approved within 5 business days of scorecard publication
l4_steps.pain_point: No system-enforced guardrail check; planner reliance on manual KPI dashboard review risks missing constraints

l4_steps.name: Run fleet assignment optimisation for shortlisted routes
l4_steps.input: Approved route shortlist, current fleet plan, aircraft availability calendar
l4_steps.output: Fleet assignment plan with gauge recommendations per route
l4_steps.kpi: Fleet utilisation uplift ≥2% vs current plan in optimised output
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyMAX optimisation assumes unconstrained maintenance slots; MRO visit conflicts discovered post-optimisation require manual iteration

l4_steps.name: Assess slot & airport capacity constraints
l4_steps.input: Fleet assignment plan, IATA WSG slot library for target airports
l4_steps.output: Slot feasibility report (available, historic grandfather, needs application)
l4_steps.kpi: Slot feasibility assessment completed ≥90 days before IATA scheduling conference
l4_steps.pain_point: Slot availability at Level 3 airports (LHR, AMS, CDG) is opaque until conference; strategic plans regularly revised post-conference

l4_steps.name: Evaluate airport infrastructure & ground handling readiness
l4_steps.input: Slot feasibility report, proposed frequencies, aircraft gauge
l4_steps.output: Airport readiness assessment (gates, ground handlers, customs, fuelling)
l4_steps.kpi: Infrastructure gap identified ≥12 months before proposed launch date
l4_steps.pain_point: Ground handler capacity data at outstations not centrally held; planner must contact handlers individually, adding 3–6 weeks to cycle

l4_steps.name: Confirm operational feasibility of candidate routes
l4_steps.input: Fleet assignment plan, slot feasibility report, airport readiness assessment
l4_steps.output: Operationally feasible route set confirmed in SkyWORKS schedule editor
l4_steps.kpi: ≥80% of shortlisted routes confirmed feasible without major constraint
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew base restrictions and FAR Part 117 duty-time rules reduce feasible rotations, particularly for ultra-long-haul additions

l4_steps.name: Build unit revenue & yield forecast per candidate route
l4_steps.input: Confirmed feasible route set, demand scenarios, competitive fare data from ATPCO
l4_steps.output: PRASM and RASM forecast per route across base/upside/downside scenarios
l4_steps.kpi: RASM forecast accuracy within ±8% of actuals on launched routes (tracked retrospectively)
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM is calibrated on existing routes; forecast reliability for new O&D markets with no booking history is low — often requires manual analyst override

l4_steps.name: Model direct operating costs per route
l4_steps.input: Fleet assignment plan (aircraft type, block hours), fuel price assumptions, airport charges schedule
l4_steps.output: CASM breakdown per route (fuel, airport, crew, maintenance, overhead allocation)
l4_steps.kpi: CASM model completed within 10 business days of receiving fleet assignment input
l4_steps.pain_point: Airport charge schedules for new markets are not always available in SAP master data; finance team must source bilaterally from airport authorities

l4_steps.name: Assess route contribution margin and breakeven load factor
l4_steps.input: RASM forecast, CASM breakdown, targeted load factor assumptions
l4_steps.output: Route P&L summary with breakeven load factor and payback period
l4_steps.kpi: Target contribution margin ≥12% in Year 2; breakeven load factor ≤75%
l4_steps.pain_point: Sensitivity of breakeven load factor to fuel price is high; +10% fuel swing shifts breakeven by 4–6 ppts, making many routes marginal

l4_steps.name: Aggregate network business case for plan period
l4_steps.input: Individual route P&L summaries, network-level synergy assumptions (feed, connectivity)
l4_steps.output: 3-year network business case document (revenue, cost, EBIT impact)
l4_steps.kpi: Network EBIT uplift ≥$150M over plan period vs do-nothing baseline
l4_steps.pain_point: Network synergy benefits (connecting traffic uplift) are difficult to isolate and often overstated in bottom-up aggregation

l4_steps.name: Package strategic plan for governance review
l4_steps.input: Network business case, route scorecard, risk register
l4_steps.output: Executive briefing pack: network strategy summary, investment ask, risk matrix
l4_steps.kpi: Briefing pack issued ≥5 business days before Network Strategy Committee meeting
l4_steps.pain_point: Version control of the briefing pack is manual; late assumption changes from Revenue Management or Finance require last-minute slides rebuild

l4_steps.name: Present plan to Network Strategy Committee
l4_steps.input: Executive briefing pack, committee member pre-read questions
l4_steps.output: Committee decision: approved / approved with conditions / rejected with rationale
l4_steps.kpi: Committee decision reached in ≤2 review cycles (no more than 1 deferral per plan)
l4_steps.pain_point: Committee quorum requires C-suite attendance; scheduling conflicts routinely delay decision by 2–4 weeks, compressing scheduling window

l4_steps.name: Publish approved strategic network plan & handoff to scheduling
l4_steps.input: Approved committee decision, final route list with gauge and frequency targets
l4_steps.output: Published strategic network plan loaded into SkyWORKS as planning baseline for Schedule Planning team
l4_steps.kpi: Plan published in SkyWORKS ≤3 business days after committee approval
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS baseline lock-in creates downstream rigidity; late executive changes after publication require formal change request and delay tactical planning
